matches.description: Watch Rio Ave vs GIL Vicente highlights and goals from Primeira Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 3, 2026. The Primeira Liga calendar brought Rio Ave and Gil Vicente together on May 3, 2026 , for a contest where tactical discipline and defensive organization took center stage. Both sides entered the pitch looking to climb the table, setting the scene for a hard-fought encounter in Vila do Conde. A Cagey Opening Exchange The match began with both teams struggling to find their rhythm in the final third. Rio Ave looked to assert themselves early, but Gustavo Mancha was caught in an offside position just four minutes in, setting a tone for a half defined by near-misses and defensive resilience. A significant scare for the visitors arrived in the 10th minute when a defensive blunder by Luis Esteves nearly gifted Rio Ave an opening, though the hosts were unable to capitalize on the mistake. As the first half progressed, the game became a battle of set-pieces. Marios Vrousai and Nelson Abbey delivered several dangerous corners for Rio Ave , while Ghislain Konan provided the service for Gil Vicente . Despite the frequent dead-ball opportunities, neither goalkeeper was truly tested before the interval. Tamble Monteiro and Dario Spikic both attempted long-range efforts to break the deadlock, but their shots failed to trouble the target, leaving the match scoreless as the teams retreated to the dressing rooms. Defensive Resilience and Tactical Shifts The second half saw an increase in intensity as both managers looked to their benches to spark a breakthrough. Gil Vicente introduced Agustin ira at the restart, and the substitute immediately looked to stretch the home defense. However, it was Rio Ave who came closest to scoring just after the hour mark. In a quick succession of chances, Jalen Blesa and Francisco Petrasso both connected with powerful headers from corner deliveries, but Gil Vicente goalkeeper Daniel Figueira was equal to the task, making two comfortable saves to keep his clean sheet intact. The physical nature of the game intensified as the clock ticked down, leading to a series of bookings. Ryan Guilherme was cautioned for a rough challenge in the 63rd minute, followed shortly by Ze Ferreira , who saw yellow for a shirt-pull. A flurry of late substitutions followed, with Sergio Bermejo , Ole Pohlmann , and Carlos Eduardo entering the fray as both sides searched for a late winner amid a sea of tactical adjustments. Stoppage Time Heartbreak The game reached a fever pitch in the four minutes of added time. Gil Vicente nearly snatched all three points in the 93rd minute when Agustin ira found space in the box, only to see his clinical finish bounce agonizingly off the post. The drama didn't end there, as Sergio Bermejo launched a desperate effort from outside the area in the 95th minute that whistled just wide of the frame. Despite the late pressure from the visitors, who finished the match with 56% possession, the Rio Ave defense held firm. The referee blew the final whistle shortly after a failed counter-attack from the hosts, confirming a stalemate that, while lacking in goals, provided plenty of tension for the supporters in attendance. On 2026-05-12 , the Primeira Liga spotlight turned to the clash between Gil Vicente and Arouca , as both sides sought to climb the table in a high-stakes encounter. The atmosphere was charged with anticipation as fans gathered to witness a tactical battle that promised to unfold with intensity and drama. A Strategic Stalemate in the First Half The match began with Gil Vicente looking to impose their rhythm early on, as Murilo tested the waters with a header just two minutes in. However, the attempt failed to find the target, setting the tone for a first half defined more by defensive discipline than offensive clinicality. As the minutes ticked by, both teams struggled to break the deadlock, with offside calls against Marvin Gilbert and Agustin ira thwarting the hosts' advances, while Javi Sanchez was caught straying for Arouca . Discipline became a factor as the half progressed, with Agustin ira receiving a yellow card for Gil Vicente in the 22nd minute, followed by Arouca's Jose Fontan getting booked shortly before the break. Despite a late header from Ivan Barbero that forced a comfortable save from Daniel Figueira , the first 45 minutes concluded without a breakthrough, leaving everything to be decided in the second period. Explosion of Goals After the Interval The game transformed completely after the restart, ignited by a flurry of goals that shifted the momentum back and forth. In the 61st minute, Arouca finally broke the silence when Bas Kuipers rose highest to head home a precise delivery from Javi Sanchez . The lead was short-lived, however, as Gil Vicente responded almost immediately. Just two minutes later, Luis Esteves unleashed a stunning strike from outside the box, assisted by Gustavo Varela , to level the score and send the home crowd into a frenzy. The parity didn't last long. In the 67th minute, Pablo Gozalbez turned provider, setting up Ivan Barbero who finished clinically with his right foot to restore Arouca's advantage. As Gil Vicente pushed for another equalizer, Arouca capitalized on the space left behind. In the 82nd minute, Taichi Fukui delivered the decisive blow, firing a powerful right-footed shot from distance into the back of the net after being set up by substitute Dylan Nandin . Late Pressure and Final Whistle With the clock winding down, the tension escalated. Gil Vicente introduced Carlos Eduardo and Martin Fernandez in an attempt to salvage a result, but Ignacio de Arruabarrena remained focused in the Arouca goal, saving a header from Fernandez in the 84th minute. The closing stages were marred by a heavy challenge from Hector Hernandez , who received a yellow card for a foul on Jose Fontan , adding to the physical nature of the contest. In stoppage time, Gil Vicente threw everything forward, with Marvin Gilbert seeing a header blocked and Martin Fernandez firing wide. Despite the late pressure and a series of corners, the Arouca defense, led by the resilient Javi Sanchez , held firm. When the referee blew the final whistle at the 90+6' mark, it was Arouca who celebrated a hard-fought victory, having controlled 55% of the possession in a clinical second-half display.
